articles.title: Northampton seek ‘happy medium’ after Hearn claims Pollock worth £1m a year
articles.summary: Player’s representative pushes for seven-figure salary. Phil Dowson insists ‘the appetite is for him to stay’ The Northampton director of rugby, Phil Dowson, has said the club “have have got to find a happy medium” in contract talks with Henry Pollock after the player’s representative, Eddie Hearn…
body: Pollock is said to earn around £150,000 a season and his current deal expires at the end of the 2026-27 campaign. Hearn has stated Pollock could earn “10 times” that if he were to move to another club, warning “he can’t stay at the club on the money he’s on”.

The 21-year-old has 13 England caps but has made just one start. Hearn says his commercial profile warrants a seven-figure salary. Pollock is among the 25 England players to receive an enhanced contract worth £150,000 and Dowson expressed confidence the reigning Prem champions can keep hold of him.

He said: “It is going well. We are still pushing it through. What Eddie Hearn also said, and people have gone straight to the million-pound remark, but the other thing he said is that Henry wants to win stuff, Henry wants to stay at Saints, Henry wants to play with that group of players. He wants to win the World Cup. I embrace that. I am all for that. The appetite is for him to stay. Now, we’ve got to find a happy medium. We really want to keep him, he really wants to stay, and that’s a great start.

articles.title: 'Zero excuses' - Wardley out to avenge Dubois loss
articles.summary: Fabio Wardley says there are "zero excuses" heading into his highly anticipated rematch with WBO heavyweight champion Daniel Dubois on 17 October.
body: Wardley, 31, dropped fellow Briton Dubois twice when they fought in May but was stopped in round 11 and lost his world title.
The Ipswich fighter immediately triggered his rematch clause and will look to avenge the only defeat of his career at London's O2 Arena.
"I have zero excuses for the loss on the night and zero excuses going into the rematch," Wardley said at Wednesday's launch news conference.
"By no means did I expect to get through boxing unscathed - not many do. Even Daniel has proven you can take a loss and come back, he's a two-time heavyweight champion."

articles.title: Tiger Woods handed five-year driving ban after no-contest plea over crash
articles.summary: Woods pleads no contest to reduced charge. Charges stemmed from March rollover crash. Tiger Woods pleaded no contest to reckless driving on Wednesday morning as part of an agreement with Florida prosecutors that reduced a DUI charge stemming from his rollover crash in March.
body: The 50-year-old was adjudicated guilty of willful and wanton reckless driving, a second offense, during a hearing in Martin County court. Under the agreement, Woods was fined $1,000 and had his driver’s license suspended for five years. Prosecutors had originally charged him with driving under the influence with property damage.

Woods also pleaded no contest to refusing to submit to a lawful test and was fined $500 on that count. He received a concurrent five-year license suspension on a careless-driving citation and agreed not to seek a hardship exemption during the suspension. Court records show he paid $2,131.44 in fines and costs following Wednesday’s hearing.
The plea agreement brings an end to the criminal case arising from the golfer’s crash near his Florida home on Jupiter Island. He had previously pleaded not guilty to both charges.

Woods, dressed in ⁠a dark suit and tie, arrived at the Martin County Courthouse seated in the front passenger seat of ​a black SUV. He did not answer questions ‌from the gathered reporters as ‌he and his girlfriend, Vanessa Trump, walked in and out of the building for the change of plea hearing.

articles.title: How Everton's deadline day debacle leaves owners facing fan mutiny
articles.summary: Everton's transfer deadline day debacle over Folarin Balogun leaves owners The Friedkin facing fan mutiny, says chief football writer Phil McNulty.
body: Everton 's shambolic end to the transfer window has resulted in open revolt from supporters that places fierce scrutiny on owners The Friedkin Group and chief executive Angus Kinnear.

The last straw for fans already infuriated by the controversial proposed sale of home-grown youngster Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest - the deal was eventually blocked by Everton 's board in the face of the toxic reaction from the fanbase - was the bungled final day before the window closed.

Folarin Balogun's proposed £40m move from AS Monaco descended into high farce in the early hours of Wednesday morning after the original deal was renegotiated when issues arose with his medical, ending with the United States striker deciding to walk away from Everton's Finch Farm training base without signing.
And all after Balogun, 25, and both clubs had signed the deal sheet allowing the move to be completed after Tuesday's 23.00 BST transfer deadline.

articles.title: 'I'll bet on this' - Vrancken backs Braga to stay at Hearts
articles.summary: Head coach Wouter Vrancken would wager on Claudio Braga remaining at Hearts and thinks a second full season at Tynecastle can enhance the striker's chances of a big move.
body: "He is fully focused here, fully committed," said the Belgian of the 26-year-old.
When asked if the Portuguese would still be at the club when the transfer window closes on Thursday, Vrancken added with a chuckle: "I think he will be here. I'll bet on this.
"But you never know, so let's hope that we can keep him because he has a lot of value for the team."
Braga has scored twice and provided three assists in 10 outings this term while he hit the net 17 times during his first campaign in Edinburgh, having been signed from the Norwegian second tier.

articles.title: Hampshire make Kuggeleijn U-turn after criticism
articles.summary: Hampshire decide that New Zealand all-rounder Scott Kuggeleijn will not represent the club having "listened to feedback from staff and supporters".
body: On Tuesday the Rose and Crown named him in their squad for a County Championship match against Warwickshire without announcing his signing on their social channels.
The signing received criticism on social media and less than an hour before the start of play on Wednesday the county said that Kuggeleijn would not play any role in their final four games.
Kuggeleijn, 34, faced a rape charge in 2015 and after a re-trial due to a hung jury he was acquitted in 2017.
It is understood that the player was in attendance at Utilita Bowl for the first day of the game on Wednesday.

articles.title: What Can Corey Kiner Bring to the Patriots As RB3?
articles.summary: New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel admitted to concerns about his team’s depth following their preseason finale. The Patriots relied heavily on backups throughout the preseason, hoping to build depth and uncover hidden contributors.
body: On August 29, the Patriots traded for Arizona Cardinals second-year running back Corey Kiner. With roster cutdowns complete, Kiner is one of three remaining running backs on New England's active roster.
Although Kiner's NFL experience is limited, the film shows promise as a physical back who can help keep the Patriots on schedule in 2026.

Kiner entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2025, spending training camp with the San Francisco 49ers before joining the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad. He didn't reach the Cardinals' active roster until December, when injuries opened an opportunity in Arizona's backfield.
Kiner appeared in four games for the Cardinals, logging 12 carries for 58 yards. The production was modest, but efficient, and his contact balance stood out most.

articles.title: The Vikings Snagged a Pair of Bruisers
articles.summary: A football roster is always in the process of being adjusted. However, the degree of roster change in late August and early September is particularly notable. Things are no different in Minnesota. Yesterday, the Vikings snagged a pair of newcomers.
body: Note that Minnesota went into these decisions with an open spot on the practice squad. As a result, going +2 with new players alongside just a -1 made the math work.

In Cam Grandy, the Vikings are welcoming a tight end who boasts good size. He’s a sturdy 6’5″ and 253 pounds (but a spot like PFF lists him as being a touch larger, coming in at 260 on there). For comparison, T.J. Hockenson is listed as being 6’5″ and 248 pounds. Josh Oliver, meanwhile, is a hulking 6’5″ and 264 pounds.
A large part of the intrigue for the 26-year-old tight end is that he has demanded respect in the past for his blocking.

In 2024, Grandy earned a 74.9 pass blocking grade on PFF. He then upped the ante in 2025 with a 77.0 PFF grade. As a run blocker, the grades aren’t quite so promising — 65.6 and then 61.0 — but there’s promise here for the well-built TE.

With Lawson stepping up to be Max Verstappen's team-mate at Red Bull, Yuki Tsunoda will have another chance to impress at Racing Bulls.

Red Bull only made the decision on Wednesday afternoon to give Hadjar every chance to drive but medical staff have decided he should miss another event and hope to return for the following race in Madrid next weekend.
"Liam will drive alongside Max at the Italian Grand Prix in Monza, while Isack continues to make encouraging progress following the wrist injury sustained during the summer break," said Red Bull.

articles.title: Mark Walter Has Thrust Chelsea into a Vortex of Uncertainty
articles.summary: Another Premier League season is officially underway, and despite the usual dose of high hopes for Chelsea, the flagship football club finds itself embroiled in more uncertainty than it ever expected.
body: Minority stakeholders Mark Walter and Todd Boehly, who own a combined 26 percent (13 percent apiece) of Chelsea, are reportedly in talks to sell their shares to Clearlake Capital, which already controls around 61.5 percent of the franchise. To be sure, the talks between Boehly and Clearlake, specifically, are not new. The sides have discussed an ownership stake exchange in the past, albeit to no avail.

This time around, however, another is added to the equation: Walter, who recently sold the NBA’s Los Angeles Lakers and also owns MLB’s Los Angeles Dodgers, is under federal investigation for misreporting what’s known as related-party loans among his own business ventures. Though nothing has been finalized, Walter’s dilemma injects previously unheard-of urgency into the equation.

articles.title: Swing Changes Fail When Golfers Rush The Fix
articles.summary: The Trap of Immediate Results. Most golfers ruin a good swing change before it even sticks. They make one adjustment and expect instant perfection. When the ball doesn’t fly straight on the first try, they panic.
body: Next time you see a player struggle after a tweak, look for the return of old patterns. It is a common struggle for amateurs and pros alike. The real test is whether they stick to the plan. Fans should expect some rough patches as players adjust. The ones who survive this phase are the ones who improve their game. Patience is the only real shortcut to a better swing.
points: Most golfers ruin a good swing change before it even sticks.

articles.title: Cameron says talks are 'advanced' to fight Shields
articles.summary: Chantelle Cameron says that talks for her to fight Claressa Shields are advanced and moving quickly following her victory over Mikaela Mayer.
body: Cameron defeated Mayer by unanimous decision in a thriller to become WBA, WBC and WBO super-welterweight world champion at MPW-06 in Birmingham on Saturday.

She emerged victorious, edging a tight contest 97-93, 97-93, 96-94 on the judges' scorecards, further glossing a stellar resume that already honours her as the only woman to ever defeat the great Katie Taylor in her professional career.
With the victory strengthening Cameron's claim to a place among the greats of the women's game, she now has eyes on taking on the self-proclaimed 'GWOAT' [Greatest woman of all time] in Shields.

Many thought a rematch with Mayer would be next on her list, but Cameron told Sky Sports that things are moving rapidly with the WBC and WBA middleweight champion, who has a record of 19-0 across multiple weight divisions.

articles.title: MVG starts World Series of Darts Finals defence against Ilagan
articles.summary: Michael van Gerwen will open his World Series of Darts Finals title defence against Lourence Ilagan, as Luke Littler goes head-to-head with Danny Noppert in Amsterdam.
body: Reigning champion Van Gerwen celebrated his sixth World Series Finals crown 12 months ago, and the top seed will mark his return to the Dutch capital against two-time PDC Asian Champion Ilagan.

The opening round will take place across two sessions on September 17-18, as 2024 champion Littler kicks off his campaign against former UK Open champion Noppert as he continues his quest for a major clean sweep.

World number two Luke Humphries also faces Dutch opposition in Jermaine Wattimena, while Gerwyn Price opens his bid for a third World Series Finals title against Australian Darts Masters runner-up Brody Klinge.
Dutch number one Gian van Veen meets former Masters champion Chris Dobey in another eye-catching affair, while Stephen Bunting and Josh Rock lock horns for a place in round two.
